title: How do we change inches and square inches to centimetres?
description: One inch is two point five four centimetres, so inches are changed to centimetres by multiplying and centimetres to inches by dividing. A square inch is a square with each side one inch, so its area is two point five four times two point five four square centimetres. Keeko takes one square inch as two point five four square centimetres.
teaching_notes: One idea: changing a length multiplies or divides by 2.54, and changing an area needs 2.54 twice because a square has two sides. Watch for students who convert a square unit with the length factor alone.

source: Convert 5 in to centimetres, 11.43 cm to inches, and 1 in2 to square centimetres, using 1 in = 2.54 cm
video_script.why: The child can multiply and divide decimals and knows that one inch is two point five four centimetres, and now changes a square unit.
video_script.substitution: The numbers five inches and eleven point four three centimetres come from the book's own conversions.
video_script.anchor: a school ruler with inches on one edge and centimetres on the other
video_script.wrong_answer: two point five four square centimetres
video_script.wrong_move: Keeko says one square inch is two point five four square centimetres, using the length factor once. A square inch has two sides of two point five four centimetres, so it is two point five four times two point five four.
video_script.payoff_line: Five inches is twelve point seven centimetres. Eleven point four three centimetres is four point five inches. One square inch is six point four five one six square centimetres.

final_answer.spoken: twelve point seven centimetres, four point five inches and six point four five one six square centimetres

maths_rules: Keeko: 2.54 cm2 is a strip 2.54 cm long and 1 cm wide; the square needs 2.54 such strips
video_script.design: A ruler with inches on one edge and centimetres on the other stays on the board. A one inch square is drawn on it with both sides marked two point five four centimetres. Keeko's strip is drawn along one side of the square.

<bookmark mark='round'/>Step four, check by rounding two point five four to two and a half.
<bookmark mark='one'/>Five times two and a half is twelve and a half.
<bookmark mark='two'/>Eleven point four divided by two and a half is about four point six.
<bookmark mark='three'/>Two and a half times two and a half is six and a quarter.

narration: <bookmark mark='doubt'/>Keeko thinks one square inch is two point five four square centimetres.
<bookmark mark='strip'/>But that area is only a thin strip, one centimetre wide, along one side.
